cues: Antibiotics are broad or narrow spectrum, and either kill bacteria or just stop them growing.
Every one of them hits something only bacteria have: the cell wall, the bacterial ribosome, bacterial enzymes.
That is why antibiotics are useless against a cold or flu.
And resistance spreads between bacteria on plasmids, driven by antibiotics sold without prescription and courses left unfinished.
